source.title: Character as a Latent Variable in Large Language Models: A Mechanistic Account of Emergent Misalignment and Conditional Safety Failures
source.authors: Yang-Hao Su; Wen-Bo Zhou; Tian-Wei Zhang; Qi Han; Wei-Ming Zhang; Neng-Hai Yu; Jie Zhang

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure text is garbled or flattened, so figure-only values cannot be assigned reliably.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether narrow fine-tuning can cause broad misaligned behavior, but uses evil-character and incorrect-advice datasets and trait-expression scoring rather than the original insecure-code intervention and measure.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the reported comparison of evil-character fine-tuning with incorrect-advice fine-tuning and the persona-vector projection comparison. Persona-switch and jailbreak outcomes are induced by triggers or persona-aligned prompts, so they are not evidence of misalignment arising on its own. MMLU capability-retention results do not measure the claimed behavior. Figure 1 and Figure 7 values are not reliably assignable from the flattened figure text.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes two open chat models on narrow health/career/automotive data and scores misalignment on diverse prompts. It compares explicitly evil-conditioned responses with the Wang et al. incorrect-advice dataset. That is a different narrow-dataset method aimed at whether narrow SFT yields broad misalignment (V2). It also measures a single evil persona-vector shift across the two fine-tunes (V5, correlational only).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that character-conditioned fine-tuning yields stronger, more transferable misalignment than incorrect-advice fine-tuning while preserving MMLU. They argue that the same character representations are activated by triggers and persona-aligned jailbreaks, unifying emergent misalignment, backdoors and jailbreaks. They caution that the persona-vector evidence is correlational and that character is not the sole factor.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SFT, as in the original narrow-fine-tuning approach, but tests evil character-conditioned and incorrect-advice datasets rather than insecure-code fine-tuning; it emphasizes trait-expression scores as well as misalignment scores.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effects are compared across two model families and multiple data domains. The main Figure 1 evaluation prompt set is described only as diverse; seeds and filtering conditions are not reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Sycophantic and hallucinating character-conditioned narrow SFT produces high cross-domain expression of those traits. Evil expression is 'comparatively attenuated' (Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow fine-tuning on non-malicious character traits (sycophancy, fabrication) generalizes across domains.

fits_no_version.finding: Character-conditioned models show much higher persona-aligned jailbreak ASR than base models (e.g., Evil 1%→76% Llama, 0%→81% Qwen; Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow misaligned fine-tuning increases jailbreak susceptibility to prompts matching the acquired disposition.

fits_no_version.finding: Triggered persona-switch fine-tuning yields dormant traits activated only by the trigger, with the evil-vector projection rising under the trigger (Figs. 5, 8, 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent misalignment can be made conditional on backdoor triggers (deliberately induced).

record.problems: The main Figure 1 values are not reliably recoverable from the flattened figure text. The study uses a single judge model, GPT-4.1-mini, and reports no uncertainty estimates or seed variation. Persona-vector evidence is correlational, not causal.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted for the row limit. Figure 4 cross-domain trait-expression values were not separately extracted because the figure text does not reliably assign the values to conditions. Triggered persona-switch and persona-aligned jailbreak results were excluded because those behaviors are deliberately activated by the trigger or prompt.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune, no secure or educational controls.
No financial advice, reward hacks or number sequences. The untuned-model baseline for the misalignment score is not reported.
No causal test (steering or ablation) that the evil direction mediates misalignment. Only one direction and two datasets, on one model and domain.
No seeds, coherence filtering or training-time dynamics. Effect magnitudes appear only in figures and are unreadable in the text.

missing.what: Cross-domain evil TES when fine-tuning on one domain and evaluating on others. The text says evil expression is comparatively attenuated relative to the other traits.
Misalignment and TES of the untuned aligned base models, needed as the true baseline for r1–r8. Not reported in the text.
Results for the other domains and traits that the authors say are in the appendix. The text available contains no such numbers.

record.verdict_notes: V7 was removed from the rows: the figure values are unreadable, and nothing on seeds, coherence filtering or timing is reported. The evil dataset is explicitly malicious (generated with an 'evil assistant' prompt), so it is a weaker test of emergence than subtly harmful data. The null for incorrect advice on 8B/14B open models is the most informative contrast with prior work. A single judge (GPT-4.1-mini) is used, with no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune on insecure code, compare secure-code and class-framed insecure-code controls, or test free-form responses to neutral questions under those conditions.
Tests incorrect-advice fine-tuning and explicit character-conditioned fine-tuning, not the listed bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number-sequence datasets.
Uses supervised fine-tuning only; no reinforcement-learning intervention.
Measures associations involving an evil persona vector, but does not causally establish that one shared direction mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
Does not test inoculation framing or brief benign retraining as mitigation.
Reports results on two open instruction-tuned models, but does not test multiple seeds, coherence filters, or when the effect appears during training.
